question.problem: Compute the eigenvalues of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 13 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].$

current_example.problem: Compute the eigenvalues of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131545/assets/29740c948e92fa88b872a1fb8a5b1b92bc103a9f25238cb2e553445c37204639.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\, A-\lambda I \mathbin{:}$

﻿﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131545/assets/5164357e31cd067e651802ab8e0a6c370335620a9c6696c55f68ffeaa8eb6b9e.svg)

Then, we compute the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-2(-2) & =0 \\ 1-2\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \\  & =\frac{-(-2)\pm \sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4(1)(5)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{-16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2\pm 4\text{i}}{2} \\  & =1\pm 2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda=1\pm 2\textrm{i}.$
